item.title: More kids ditching their phones to find summer jobs
item.description: Meet the children leaving their devices behind this summer to flex their entrepreneurial muscles with summer jobs.

item.title: Senate committee votes to hold Fauci in contempt of Congress
item.description: The Senate Homeland Security Committee voted to hold Dr. Anthony Fauci in contempt of Congress over his refusal to answer questions during testimony before the committee last week.

item.title: What's at stake for Democrats in next week's Wisconsin primary
item.description: More states will hold primary elections next week, including Wisconsin, where democratic socialist Francesca Hong is leading several polls in her run for governor. CBS News' Zak Hudak takes a look at the race as the countdown to the midterm elections continues.

item.title: Trump issues new executive orders aimed at birthright citizenship
item.description: The Supreme Court in June struck down President Trump's earlier executive order aimed at ending birthright citizenship.

item.title: Growing wave of cyber scams cost Americans nearly $150 billion in 2025
item.description: Matt Gutman reports on how he almost fell for a scam involving his bank as more Americans are becoming victims to similar cyber crimes each year.

item.title: Privacy groups raise red flags over police misuse of Flock cameras
item.description: Privacy groups are expressing concerns over Flock cameras, the devices that capture license plates and are often used in criminal investigations. They argue that police may be using them for improper reasons. Mark Strassman reports.

item.title: Star Cambridge professor resigns amid plagiarism allegations
item.description: Jason Arday, who joined Cambridge in 2023 at the age of 37, became one of Britain's most high-profile academics after sharing an extraordinary life story.

item.title: Are Trump's new executive orders targeting birthright citizenship constitutional?
item.description: President Trump on Thursday signed two executive orders aimed at curbing birthright citizenship. In June, the Supreme Court struck down a broader executive order meant to end birthright citizenship. CBS News legal contributor Jessica Levinson has more.

item.title: Cambridge's youngest Black professor resigns amid allegations of plagiarism
item.description: Jason Arday, who made history as Cambridge's youngest Black professor, has resigned after accusations of plagiarism and fabrications in his biography. Arday has denied any deliberate wrongdoing. Holly Williams has the details.

item.title: Woman hospitalized after being struck by car driven by young children
item.description: Police say two children under the age of 10 stole and crashed their parents' car in Oakland, California, on Thursday, sending a woman and themselves to the hospital. Da Lin reports.

item.title: Trump doubles down on fight against birthright citizenship with new executive orders
item.description: On Thursday, President Trump signed two new executive orders to limit birthright citizenship, about a month after the Supreme Court ended his previous effort. Weija Jiang has more.

item.title: How to limit your exposure to foodborne illnesses, according to an infectious disease specialist
item.description: Several states are reporting outbreaks of foodborne illnesses stemming from salmonella and cyclospora. Dr. Peter Chin-Hong, an infectious disease specialist at the University of California, San Francisco, joins CBS News with food safety tips.

item.title: How Trump's new birthright citizenship orders differ from what Supreme Court struck down
item.description: President Trump on Thursday signed executive orders to limit birthright citizenship after the Supreme Court struck down his previous effort. CBS News legal contributor Jessica Levinson joins with analysis.

item.title: Proposed agreement between Iran and Oman on Strait of Hormuz could complicate supply chains
item.description: A proposed deal between Iran and Oman could give Tehran more control over who enters the Strait of Hormuz and complicate access to the vital waterway for the shipping industry. Gene Seroka, executive director for the Port of Los Angeles, joins CBS News to discuss.

item.title: FAA orders inspections of 737 Max jets after cracks found in older planes
item.description: The Federal Aviation Administration has ordered inspections of hundreds of Boeing 737 Max jets after cracks were found in parts of some older model Boeing planes.

item.title: Republican-led Senate committee votes to hold Fauci in contempt over silence in COVID hearing
item.description: A Senate committee led by Republicans has voted to hold Dr. Anthony Fauci in contempt over his refusal to answer questions during last week's congressional hearing on the COVID pandemic. Caitlin Huey-Burns has the story.

item.title: A timeline of Trump's threats and backtracks against Iran
item.description: President Trump has a history of threatening major attacks against Iran and then backtracking. CBS News national security analyst Aaron MacLean has more.

item.title: Best debt relief companies, plus advice borrowers need to know now
item.description: These debt relief companies could help you slash your debt, but there are some things to know before signing up.

item.title: FAA orders inspections on hundreds of Boeing 737 Max jets for fuselage cracks
item.description: Federal regulators have ordered nearly 500 Boeing jets in the U.S. to be inspected for cracks in the fuselage. Kris Van Cleave has the details.

item.title: Minnesota Chipotle burrito bowl meal led to sepsis hospitalization, lawsuit says
item.description: A Minnesota woman says she fainted, spiked a 102-degree fever, and was hospitalized with sepsis three days after eating a chicken burrito bowl at a Chipotle in Roseville, and genetic testing connected her case to a multistate outbreak, according to a lawsuit filed Tuesday.

item.title: Company's safety record raises questions after Los Angeles food warehouse fire
item.description: A CBS News investigation into last month's massive food warehouse fire in Los Angeles is raising questions about a cold storage company linked to the warehouse. CBS News' Matt Gutman reports.

item.title: Spokane arson suspect had planned devastating wildfire for weeks, police say
item.description: Police said a man charged with starting a wildfire confessed to the crime, describing how he planned it for weeks and created a device to ignite a blaze that destroyed hundreds of buildings.

item.title: FBI says hackers altered operating instructions for water systems in some states
item.description: At least 12 states are reporting cyberattacks on water systems that may be linked to Iran-backed hackers. CBS News homeland security correspondent Nicole Sganga has the latest.

item.title: Centrist Democrat group plans $15 million effort against Democratic Socialists of America
item.description: Republicans running against democratic socialists have found an unlikely ally: other Democrats. The centrist Democrat think tank Third Way has pledged $15 million to discredit the DSA movement between now and 2028. Third Way President Jonathan Cowan joins "The Takeout" to discuss.

item.title: Iran, Oman deal on Strait of Hormuz getting close, Tehran says
item.description: Iran and Oman are close to agreeing on new arrangements for the Strait of Hormuz, but not for a full reopening of the vital waterway, Iran's state news agency says.

item.title: Bessent announces crackdown on undocumented immigrants' use of U.S. banks
item.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told Arizona bankers the administration won't allow "risks posed by the extension of financial services to illegal aliens."

item.title: Flesh-eating bacteria has killed 5 in Louisiana this year, officials say
item.description: A flesh-eating bacteria found in warm coastal waters is responsible for at least five deaths so far this year in Louisiana, state health officials reported Thursday.

item.title: 8/6: The Takeout with Major Garrett
item.description: Rep. Haley Stevens discusses her primary loss to Abdul El-Sayed; President Trump denies reports of U.S. munitions shortages.

item.title: What Fauci has said about COVID origins, gain-of-function research
item.description: Thursday's vote to hold Dr. Anthony Fauci in contempt of Congress follows years of tension with GOP Sen. Rand Paul, hinging on the origins of the coronavirus and a controversial type of research.

item.title: Cyclospora boosts fears that deadlier foodborne outbreaks are ahead
item.description: Food safety experts say cuts to the public health system hobbled the response — and that the next outbreak could be much worse.
